> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /annealer/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /annealer/llms-full.txt.

# Introduction

annealer is a formatter that reorders HTML and Vue template attributes by their semantic meaning. It also reorders declarations in stylesheets (CSS, SCSS, Sass, Less). The order is defined by a swappable YAML profile, not hard-coded.

```html
<!-- Input -->
<a title="Home" href="/" id="home">Home</a>

<!-- Output (html profile) -->
<a id="home" title="Home" href="/">Home</a>
```

:::warning Work in progress
annealer is under active development. The npm package is not published yet, and the profile format can still change before it is declared stable.
:::

## Why attribute order matters

### Order is a code-review problem, not a cosmetic one

When several contributors edit the same component over time, attributes are added, removed and rewritten. Without a fixed rule, the attribute list gets reshuffled, and diffs pull in lines that didn't really change. A stable, rule-based order keeps a diff limited to what actually changed, which lowers the cost of review.

### Attributes carry different semantic weight

HTML attributes are not an unordered set of strings:

- Some define what an element **is** (`is`, a component name).
- Some control its **state or behavior** (`v-if`, `v-model`, `disabled`, `width`/`height`).
- Some **supplement its meaning** for a human reader (`title`, `alt`).
- Some **propagate meaning** to external systems such as assistive technology (`aria-*`).

Sorting alphabetically, or keeping the typed order, hides this structure. annealer orders attributes so that an element's semantic structure is visible in the source.

The grouping is not an arbitrary preference. The WAI-ARIA specification itself splits `aria-*` attributes into _properties_ (which don't change during use) and _states_ (which do). annealer uses this split.

### Stylesheets deserve the same treatment

CSS properties also have roles: layout, appearance, state-dependent presentation. The same "order by meaning" principle applies to declaration order.

## Relation to `vue/attributes-order`

The Vue.js Style Guide already defines a priority list for attributes, and eslint-plugin-vue implements it as `vue/attributes-order`. annealer's Vue profile starts from the same default order, so projects that move away from ESLint keep the same result.

On top of that baseline, annealer adds:

- **Same-name clustering**: the static and bound forms of one attribute stay together (`class` next to `:class`).
- **ARIA sub-ordering**: role → name → description → property → state, following the WAI-ARIA properties/states split.
- **Plain HTML support**, for projects without Vue templates.
- **Stylesheet declaration order**, delegated to [malva](https://github.com/g-plane/malva).

annealer is not a rival to `vue/attributes-order`. It inherits its design and extends it. For teams that replace ESLint with rslint or oxlint, it keeps this one piece of functionality alive.

## Why a new tool

Biome, rslint, oxlint, oxfmt and markup_fmt were evaluated. None of them reorders Vue/HTML attributes by meaning:

| Tool                                | Status                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Biome (`useSortedAttributes`, HTML) | Fixed, undocumented category split; doesn't place non-directive attributes such as `id` the way the Vue Style Guide does; shares infrastructure with a known regression (duplicated/dropped attributes). |
| rslint                              | No plans to support Vue (maintainer decision).                                                                                                                                                           |
| oxlint                              | Vue rules are about correctness only; no attribute-order rule.                                                                                                                                           |
| oxfmt                               | Can't reach template markup by design.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| markup_fmt                          | Formats Vue/Svelte/Astro templates, but has no option to reorder attributes.                                                                                                                             |

CSS property order is the exception: malva already has a configurable `declarationOrder`, so annealer delegates to it. **What annealer adds is the semantic attribute grouping. Nothing else is built from zero.**

## Scope

- Attribute reordering in HTML and in Vue 3 SFC `<template>` blocks.
- Attribute normalization: `v-bind:` → `:`, `v-on:` → `@`, camelCase → kebab-case on component props.
- Layout rules for multiline tags, equivalent to `vue/html-closing-bracket-newline`, `vue/max-attributes-per-line` (multiline), `vue/html-self-closing` (void elements always, the rest opt-in) and, opt-in, `vue/multiline-html-element-content-newline`.
- Declaration order for CSS/SCSS/Sass/Less, in `<style>` blocks and in standalone files, via malva.
- Opt-in declaration order inside static `style` attributes.
- [Disable directives](/annealer/guide/features/disable-directives.md) in markup and stylesheet comments.
- Planned: [value ordering](/annealer/guide/design/value-ordering.md) for static `class` attributes, and [library profiles](/annealer/guide/design/library-profiles.md).
- Svelte is not part of the first release. The profile-based design should allow adding it later without a redesign.

## Non-goals

- Reflowing text or indentation. Line width and indentation are left to the surrounding formatter (`rs fmt`, Prettier, …).
- Vue 2 syntax (`.sync`, `.native`, …).
- General HTML/CSS validation.
- Handling deprecated or obsolete markup (`<xmp>`, `<center>`, `<font>`, `<marquee>`, `bgcolor`, …). annealer never warns about it, removes it or replaces it. It parses such markup only as far as the surrounding document needs (for example, `<xmp>` content is raw text, so tags inside it are left alone). Detecting it is a job for a linter or validator.

## Next steps

- [Getting started](/annealer/guide/start/getting-started.md): run annealer from the CLI or from JavaScript.
- [Using with other tools](/annealer/guide/start/integration.md): configuration for Rslint/`rs fmt`, oxlint/oxfmt and Biome.
- [Limitations](/annealer/guide/start/limitations.md): what annealer does not do yet.
- [Attribute order](/annealer/guide/concepts/attribute-order.md): how attributes are classified and sorted.

# Getting started

annealer has three entry points that share the same Rust core:

- **`anyl`**: the command-line tool.
- **`annealer` (npm)**: a JavaScript API backed by WebAssembly.
- **`annealer` (Rust crate)**: the pure `format()` function.

## CLI

Build the CLI from the repository (the npm package and crate are not published yet):

```bash
cargo install --path crates/annealer
```

Then format files:

```bash
anyl src/App.vue                 # print the result
anyl --write src/**/*.vue        # format in place
anyl --check index.html          # exit 1 if a file would change
anyl --profile my-profile.yaml page.html
```

Supported inputs: `.html`, `.htm`, `.vue`, `.css`, `.scss`, `.sass`, `.less`. The language is detected from the extension, and each language uses its matching built-in profile unless `--profile` is given. See [CLI](/annealer/api/cli.md) for all options.

## JavaScript

```ts
import { format } from 'annealer';

format('<a title="Home" href="/" id="home">Home</a>');
// => '<a id="home" title="Home" href="/">Home</a>'

format(source, { language: 'vue' });
format(source, { language: 'html', profile: yamlText });
```

`format()` is synchronous. The WebAssembly binary is embedded in the package, so no loader or bundler setup is needed. See [JavaScript API](/annealer/api/javascript.md).

## Example

Input:

```html
<nav aria-label="Main" class="nav" id="nav">
  <a href="/docs" class="nav__link" aria-current="page">Docs</a>
</nav>
<input
  required
  placeholder="you@example.com"
  name="email"
  type="email"
  id="email"
  class="form__input"
  aria-describedby="email-help"
/>
```

Output with the `html` profile:

```html
<nav id="nav" class="nav" aria-label="Main">
  <a class="nav__link" href="/docs" aria-current="page">Docs</a>
</nav>
<input
  id="email"
  class="form__input"
  placeholder="you@example.com"
  type="email"
  name="email"
  required
  aria-describedby="email-help"
/>
```

- `id` and `class` come first, then supplementary (`placeholder`), semantic (`type`), key-value (`name`) and state (`required`) attributes, then ARIA.
- The multiline tag gets one attribute per line, and the closing bracket goes on its own line.
- The void element `<input>` becomes `<input />`.

## Profiles

Two profiles are built in:

| Profile | Used for                                   | Summary                                                    |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `html`  | `.html`, `.css`, `.scss`, `.sass`, `.less` | Semantic order for plain HTML.                             |
| `vue`   | `.vue`                                     | `vue/attributes-order` tiers plus annealer's sub-ordering. |

To customize, start from a built-in profile (`builtinProfile('vue')` in JavaScript, or `crates/annealer/profiles/*.yaml`) and pass your YAML with `--profile` or the `profile` option. See [Profile reference](/annealer/api/profile.md).

# Using with other tools

annealer only orders things: attributes, classes and declarations. It leaves line width and indentation to your formatter. This page shows how to combine it with the usual toolchains so that neither tool undoes the other.

The examples were checked with [Prettier](https://prettier.io/) 3.9 (through `rs fmt`), [oxfmt](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/formatter.html) 0.74, [oxlint](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter.html) 1.89 and [Biome](https://biomejs.dev/) 2.6.

## Run order

Run annealer first, then the formatter:

```bash
anyl --write src/App.vue   # 1. order
rs fmt src/App.vue         # 2. format (Prettier, oxfmt, Biome, …)
```

- None of these formatters reorders attributes or declarations, so the formatter keeps annealer's order.
- annealer formats stylesheets with malva, and malva lays out some values differently from Prettier, oxfmt and Biome (see [Limitations](/annealer/guide/start/limitations.md#stylesheets)). When the formatter runs last, its layout wins and the result is stable: running both again changes nothing.
- `anyl --check` on its own can fail on files the formatter has just written, because of those layout differences. To check order in CI, run the pipeline and look for changes instead:

```bash
git ls-files -z '*.vue' '*.html' '*.css' '*.scss' '*.less' | xargs -0 anyl --write
rs fmt                  # or: oxfmt / biome format --write .
git diff --exit-code    # fails when the order or the formatting was off
```

`anyl` doesn't walk directories or expand globs itself, so pass file paths, as `git ls-files` does above.

## Settings to align

annealer's built-in profiles use these values. Aligning the formatter with them keeps `<style>` blocks and stylesheets from flipping between two styles, and keeps the formatter's diff small:

| What                       | annealer (built-in profiles)          | Prettier / `rs fmt`              | oxfmt                | Biome                                            |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| CSS string quotes          | single (`quotes: prefer-single`)      | `singleQuote: true`              | `singleQuote: true`  | `css.formatter.quoteStyle: "single"`             |
| Indentation in stylesheets | 2 spaces (malva default)              | default                          | default              | `formatter.indentStyle: "space"`                 |
| Line width in stylesheets  | 80 (malva default)                    | default                          | `printWidth: 80`     | default                                          |
| Void elements              | `<br />` (always)                     | default                          | default              | `html.formatter.selfCloseVoidElements: "always"` |
| Attribute sorting          | annealer                              | none                             | none                 | `useSortedAttributes` off (the default)          |
| Declaration sorting        | annealer (`declarationOrder: smacss`) | none                             | none                 | `useSortedProperties` off (the default)          |
| Tailwind class sorting     | `--class-order tailwind` (opt-in)     | no `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss` | no `sortTailwindcss` | `useTailwindSortedClasses` off                   |

To use double quotes instead, change the profile rather than the formatter: copy the built-in profile (`crates/annealer/profiles/*.yaml`) and set `stylesheet.malva.quotes: prefer-double`.

### Tailwind classes: pick one sorter

annealer's `tailwind` class order follows Tailwind's own order, as `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss` and oxfmt's `sortTailwindcss` do. The order is the same, but:

- Those formatters remove duplicate classes by default. annealer keeps them unless you pass `--remove-duplicate-classes`.
- They can also sort classes inside `clsx()`/`cn()` calls and attributes you list (`:class`). annealer only orders static `class` attributes.

Use one of them, not both. If you prefer the formatter's sorter, drop `--class-order` and, for oxfmt, set `preserveDuplicates: true` if you want annealer's behavior for duplicates.

## Rslint and `rs fmt` (Rstack)

Rslint lints JavaScript and TypeScript and has no Vue template rules, so nothing in it overlaps with annealer. `rs fmt` is built on Prettier, so annealer runs before it:

```ts title="rstack.config.ts"
import { define } from 'rstack';

define.lint(({ js, ts }) => [
  { ignores: ['dist/**'] },
  js.configs.recommended,
  ts.configs.recommendedTypeChecked
]);

define.fmt({
  // annealer writes single-quoted CSS strings.
  singleQuote: true
  // Don't add `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss` when you use `anyl --class-order tailwind`.
});

define.staged({
  // annealer first, then the formatter.
  '*.{vue,html,css,scss,less}': ['anyl --write', 'rs fmt'],
  '*.sass': 'anyl --write',
  '*.{js,jsx,ts,tsx,mjs,cjs,mts,cts}': ['rs lint --fix', 'rs fmt']
});
```

```json title="package.json"
{
  "scripts": {
    "format": "git ls-files -z '*.vue' '*.html' '*.css' '*.scss' '*.less' | xargs -0 anyl --write && rs fmt"
  }
}
```

Keep the staged globs to the extensions annealer supports. Any other file is an error (`unsupported file type`).

## oxlint and oxfmt (Oxc)

oxlint's `vue` plugin only checks `<script>` code; it has no template rules such as `vue/attributes-order`. Nothing has to be turned off:

```json title=".oxlintrc.json"
{
  "$schema": "./node_modules/oxlint/configuration_schema.json",
  "plugins": ["typescript", "unicorn", "oxc", "vue"],
  "categories": { "correctness": "error" },
  "ignorePatterns": ["dist/**"]
}
```

oxfmt formats `.vue` and `.html` with its bundled Prettier and CSS/SCSS/Less natively. Its defaults differ from annealer in quotes (double) and line width (100):

```json title=".oxfmtrc.json"
{
  "$schema": "./node_modules/oxfmt/configuration_schema.json",
  "singleQuote": true,
  "printWidth": 80
}
```

`printWidth: 80` matches malva's line width for stylesheets. It applies to all files, so leave it out if you want 100 for JavaScript and rely on the run order instead. Leave `sortTailwindcss` off when annealer orders classes, or turn it on and drop `--class-order`:

```json title=".oxfmtrc.json (oxfmt sorts Tailwind classes)"
{
  "singleQuote": true,
  "sortTailwindcss": {
    "stylesheet": "./src/app.css",
    "preserveDuplicates": true
  }
}
```

Then run annealer before oxfmt:

```bash
git ls-files -z '*.vue' '*.html' '*.css' '*.scss' '*.less' | xargs -0 anyl --write
oxfmt
```

## Biome

Biome's defaults conflict with annealer in four places: tabs, double-quoted CSS strings, `<br>` without a slash, and its own sorting actions. With HTML full support turned on (needed for `.vue` files), use:

```json title="biome.json"
{
  "$schema": "./node_modules/@biomejs/biome/configuration_schema.json",
  "formatter": { "indentStyle": "space", "indentWidth": 2 },
  "css": { "formatter": { "quoteStyle": "single" } },
  "html": {
    "experimentalFullSupportEnabled": true,
    "formatter": { "selfCloseVoidElements": "always" }
  },
  "assist": {
    "actions": {
      "source": {
        "useSortedAttributes": "off",
        "useSortedProperties": "off"
      }
    }
  },
  "linter": {
    "rules": { "nursery": { "useTailwindSortedClasses": "off" } }
  }
}
```

- `useSortedAttributes` sorts attributes alphabetically in HTML and Vue, and `useSortedProperties` sorts CSS declarations. Both are off by default; the config above keeps them off explicitly, because turning them on would undo annealer's order on every `biome check --write`.
- `useTailwindSortedClasses` is a nursery rule. Turn it off when annealer orders classes.
- If you keep tabs, set `stylesheet.malva.useTabs: true` in your profile instead of changing `indentStyle`.

Then run annealer before Biome:

```bash
git ls-files -z '*.vue' '*.html' '*.css' '*.scss' '*.less' | xargs -0 anyl --write
biome check --write .
```

# Limitations

annealer is still under development. This page lists what it does not do yet, and what it doesn't do by design. Each item links to the page with the details.

## Status

- **Not published yet.** The npm package and the Rust crate aren't on the registries. Build the CLI with `cargo install --path crates/annealer`.
- **The profile format can still change** before it is declared stable (`schemaVersion: 1`).

## Supported input

- HTML, Vue 3 SFC templates, and CSS, SCSS, Sass (indented syntax) and Less. Anything else is reported as an unsupported file type.
- **Not supported:** JSX/TSX, Svelte, Astro, Angular templates, Markdown/MDX, and Vue 2 syntax (`.sync`, `.native`). Svelte is planned for later.
- In `.vue` files, `<script>`, custom blocks and templates in other languages (`<template lang="pug">`) are left alone.

## Markup

- **No DOM.** annealer reads start tags with a lexer. It doesn't validate HTML or fix broken markup. Deprecated markup (`<center>`, `bgcolor`) is parsed but never reported or changed.
- **No reflow.** annealer adds or removes line breaks only where a layout rule needs them. It never re-indents lines or wraps text to a line width; that is the formatter's job ([Using with other tools](/annealer/guide/start/integration.md)).
- **Spreads are boundaries.** Attributes don't move across `v-bind="object"`, except compile-time directives (`spreadSafe` groups). A tag with a spread can therefore stay partly unordered ([Attribute order](/annealer/guide/concepts/attribute-order.md)).
- **Same-name clusters keep source order**, except for `class`, where the static form goes before the bound one. `style` and other duplicates stay as written because their order can change behavior.

## Layout

- **Void elements are always self-closed** (`<br />`, `<hr />`, `<wbr />`). This differs from the default of `vue/html-self-closing` (`html.void: never`); set `html.void: always` there, or `void: never` in your profile.
- **Self-closing empty elements and components (`<div />`, `<MyComp />`) and `contentNewline` are off by default.** Turn them on with `--self-closing` / `--content-newline` ([Layout](/annealer/guide/features/layout.md)). `<div />` is applied in Vue templates only, because it is an unclosed start tag in plain HTML.
- `contentNewline` adds line breaks but doesn't re-indent the content. Elements that are closed implicitly (`<li>` without `</li>`) are left alone.

## Class order

- **Only static `class` attributes.** Bound `:class`, `clsx()`/`cn()` calls and values with template syntax are never read.
- **Only Tailwind is built in**, generated from Tailwind CSS 4.3 with the default theme. Your own theme values and `@utility` classes aren't known: a custom color is ordered like a theme color, and unknown classes go first ([Class order](/annealer/guide/features/class-order.md)).
- **Duplicates are kept by default**, where `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss` and oxfmt remove them. Turn on `--remove-duplicate-classes` to remove them.
- No Bootstrap class order yet.

## Stylesheets

- **Stylesheets are reformatted with malva**, not only reordered. malva's layout differs from Prettier, oxfmt and Biome in places. For example, it keeps comma-separated values (`transition`, `font-family`) on one line where they break them onto several lines. No malva option removes this difference, so `anyl --check` can fail on files a formatter has just written. Run annealer before the formatter ([Run order](/annealer/guide/start/integration.md#run-order)).
- **CSS strings use single quotes** by default (`quotes: prefer-single`). With a formatter that writes double quotes, align one of them ([Settings to align](/annealer/guide/start/integration.md#settings-to-align)).
- Vendor-prefixed declarations move only when `declarationOrder` is set. A run of declarations with a comment between them is left alone ([Stylesheets](/annealer/guide/concepts/stylesheets.md)).
- Static `style` attributes are reordered only when `stylesheet.styleAttribute` is on, and not when they contain template syntax, comments or values that don't parse as plain declarations. Bound `:style` is never touched.

## Profiles and the CLI

- **No profile composition (`extends`).** To change one setting of a built-in profile, copy the whole profile (`crates/annealer/profiles/*.yaml` or `builtinProfile()`) and edit the copy.
- **No configuration file.** Options such as `--profile`, `--class-order` and `--self-closing` are passed on every run (put them in a `package.json` script).
- **`anyl` takes file paths only.** It doesn't walk directories, expand globs or read ignore files. Pass the paths from your shell or from `git ls-files`.
- No editor extension, language server or Prettier plugin. Run annealer from the CLI, a Git hook or the JavaScript API.

---

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /annealer/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /annealer/llms-full.txt.

# Attribute order

## Tokenizer: no DOM

annealer does not build a DOM or XML tree. It finds each start tag (`<tagname` … `>` or `/>`) and splits the attribute list into name/value pairs, keeping only the quote style.

This works the same way for plain HTML and for Vue's non-XML syntax (`@click`, `#default`, `v-bind:[dynamic]`). It also avoids side effects of DOM- or XML-based parsing, such as collapsing whitespace or lowercasing tag and attribute names.

Raw-text elements, comments, `{{ }}` interpolations, SFC `<script>` blocks, custom blocks and `<template lang="…">` with a non-HTML language are skipped.

## Classification

Each attribute is classified by its **normalized key**:

| Written as                  | Key                |
| --------------------------- | ------------------ |
| `foo`, `:foo`, `v-bind:foo` | `foo`              |
| `@click`, `v-on:click`      | `v-on:click`       |
| `#item`, `v-slot:item`      | `v-slot:item`      |
| `@click.stop`, `:foo.camel` | modifiers stripped |

A profile is a list of **groups** in output order. Each group has `match` patterns: an exact name, or a prefix ending in `*`. An attribute goes to the group whose pattern fits it **most specifically**: an exact name beats any prefix, and a longer prefix beats a shorter one. Attributes that match nothing go to the single **fallback** group.

Inside a group, the order is set by `sort`:

- `source`: as written (default).
- `alphabetical`: by key.
- `listed`: by the order of the `match` patterns.

## HTML profile

| #  | Group            | Attributes                                                                                                                                                    | Sort         |
| -- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ |
| 1  | global           | `id`                                                                                                                                                          |              |
| 2  | class            | `class`                                                                                                                                                       |              |
| 3  | supplementary    | `alt`, `title`, `placeholder`                                                                                                                                 | listed       |
| 4  | semantic         | `type`, `href`, `src`, `srcset`                                                                                                                               | listed       |
| 5  | key-value        | `name`, `value`, `content`                                                                                                                                    | listed       |
| 6  | dimensions       | `width`, `height`                                                                                                                                             | listed       |
| 7  | other (fallback) | state attributes such as `disabled`, `checked`, `readonly`                                                                                                    | source       |
| 8  | aria-role        | `role`                                                                                                                                                        |              |
| 9  | aria-name        | `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`                                                                                                                               | listed       |
| 10 | aria-description | `aria-describedby`, `aria-description`, `aria-details`                                                                                                        | listed       |
| 11 | aria-property    | other `aria-*`                                                                                                                                                | source       |
| 12 | aria-state       | `aria-busy`, `aria-checked`, `aria-current`, `aria-disabled`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-grabbed`, `aria-hidden`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-pressed`, `aria-selected` | source       |
| 13 | data             | `data-*`                                                                                                                                                      | alphabetical |
| 14 | events           | `on*`                                                                                                                                                         | source       |

Why this order:

- **Supplementary attributes come right after `id`/`class`.** They describe the element for a human reader. `id` and `class` stay together at the front because that is the common idiom.
- **ARIA goes near the end.** It carries extra metadata for assistive technology that `alt`/`title` can't express. It is not the primary description of the element.
- **ARIA follows WAI-ARIA**: role → accessible name → description → properties → states.
- **`data-*` is alphabetical** because no semantic order exists for it.

## Vue profile

The Vue profile follows the default order of eslint-plugin-vue's `vue/attributes-order`, so its output always satisfies that rule:

| #  | Tier             | Attributes                                                   |
| -- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1  | Definition       | `is`, `v-is`                                                 |
| 2  | List rendering   | `v-for`                                                      |
| 3  | Conditionals     | `v-if`, `v-else-if`, `v-else`, `v-show`, `v-cloak`           |
| 4  | Render modifiers | `v-pre`, `v-once`                                            |
| 5  | Global           | `id`                                                         |
| 6  | Unique / slot    | `ref`, `key`, `slot`, `v-slot*`                              |
| 7  | Two-way binding  | `v-model*`                                                   |
| 8a | Other directives | other `v-*`                                                  |
| 8b | Other attributes | the HTML profile's groups from `class` to `data` (see above) |
| 9  | Events           | `v-on*` (`@…`)                                               |
| 10 | Content          | `v-html`, `v-text`                                           |

Tier 8 is split into other directives first, then other attributes. This matches `OTHER_DIRECTIVES` → `OTHER_ATTR` in `vue/attributes-order`. The HTML sub-ordering applies inside the other-attributes tier.

```vue
<!-- Input -->
<MyItem
  @click="select"
  :class="{ active }"
  class="item"
  v-for="item in items"
  :key="item.id"
  aria-label="Item"
  v-bind:title="item.name"
  :itemName="item.name"
/>

<!-- Output -->
<MyItem
  v-for="item in items"
  :key="item.id"
  class="item"
  :class="{ active }"
  :title="item.name"
  :item-name="item.name"
  aria-label="Item"
  @click="select"
/>
```

## Same-name clustering

Because classification uses the normalized key, the static and bound forms of one attribute get the same key and stay together. The first occurrence of a key sets the position of its cluster. No special-case logic is needed.

- For **`class`**, the static form goes before the bound form (`class="item" :class="{ active }"`).
- For **other names**, the cluster keeps the source order. Vue merges `style` and the later declaration wins. For other duplicate names it keeps only one of them. Reordering them could change behavior.
- **`v-model` is never clustered with a plain attribute of the same name** (`value="x" v-model="y"`). Its key is `v-model`, not `value`, and it stays in its own tier because two-way binding is a different concept.

## `v-bind` spreads

`v-bind="object"` is a boundary. Attributes are never moved across a spread, because that can change which value wins when the object is merged.

The exception is groups marked `spreadSafe`. These are compile-time directives (`is`, `v-for`, `v-if`/…, `v-pre`/`v-once`, custom directives) that never merge with the spread object, so they can be moved across it. Everything else stays inside its segment.

## Normalization

The Vue profile enables two rewrites, which run before classification:

- `directiveShorthand`: `v-bind:foo` → `:foo`, `v-on:click` → `@click`.
- `hyphenateComponentProps`: camelCase attribute names on component tags → kebab-case (`:itemName` → `:item-name`). Native SVG and MathML elements are not affected.



---
url: /annealer/guide/concepts/stylesheets.md
---

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /annealer/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /annealer/llms-full.txt.

# Stylesheets

annealer doesn't implement CSS property ordering itself. It delegates to [malva](https://github.com/g-plane/malva), which already has a configurable `declarationOrder`. The `stylesheet` section of a profile controls this.

Formatted inputs:

- `<style>` blocks in HTML and Vue, including `<style lang="scss">`, `lang="less"` and `lang="sass"`.
- Standalone `.css`, `.scss`, `.sass` (indented syntax) and `.less` files.

If a profile has no `stylesheet` section, stylesheets are left untouched.

## Declaration order

Both built-in profiles use:

```yaml
stylesheet:
  declarationOrder: smacss
  vendorPrefix: start
```

- `declarationOrder`: `smacss` (important, flow-affecting properties first), `concentric` (from outside the box model inward), or `alphabetical`.
- `declarationOrderGroupBy`: how declarations are split into independently sorted runs: `non-declaration` (default) or `non-declaration-and-empty-line`.

```css
/* Input */
body {
  color: #222;
  margin: 0;
  font-family: system-ui, sans-serif;
  display: flex;
}

/* Output (smacss) */
body {
  display: flex;
  margin: 0;
  color: #222;
  font-family: system-ui, sans-serif;
}
```

## Vendor prefixes: `vendorPrefix: start` \{#vendor-prefixes-vendorprefix-start}

Vendor-prefixed declarations (`-webkit-…`, `-moz-…`) are treated as separate from standard properties. They are dialects, and many were never standardized. With `start`, they go **before** the other declarations of the same run, in plain alphabetical order, with no grouping by property.

Why `start` and not `end`: a prefixed property is often an alias of the standard one, and the later declaration wins. Putting prefixes last could let a dialect override the standard value (for example, `-webkit-border-radius` with two values). `start` keeps the standard property last, as Autoprefixer's output does.

malva has no such option (it sorts by the unprefixed name). annealer re-parses malva's output and moves only the prefixed declarations. Runs match malva's sort units. A run with a comment between its declarations is left alone. The option applies only when `declarationOrder` is set. `alongside` (the default when not set) keeps malva's behavior.

## Static `style` attributes (opt-in) \{#static-style-attributes-opt-in}

`stylesheet.styleAttribute: true` also orders the declarations inside static `style` attributes. It is off in both built-in profiles.

- The value stays on one line.
- CSS strings use the quote opposite to the attribute's quote. With the usual double-quoted attribute, that is the single quote annealer prefers anyway.
- A missing trailing `;` stays missing.
- Bound `:style` is never touched.
- Values are left as written when they are unquoted, contain template syntax, comments, `{}`, `<` or `&`, or don't parse as plain declarations.

## Other malva options

Other malva options go under `stylesheet.malva` (for example `printWidth`, `quotes`, `hexCase`). Unknown keys are rejected, so a typo isn't silently ignored. See the [Profile reference](/annealer/api/profile.md#stylesheet).

## Quotes

CSS strings use single quotes (`@use 'sass:math'`, `font-family: 'Noto Sans'`), as Prettier and oxfmt write them with `singleQuote`. A string keeps double quotes where single quotes would need escaping (`"O'Brien"`). This is annealer's default (`quotes: prefer-single`); malva's own default is double quotes. Set `stylesheet.malva.quotes` to change it.



---
url: /annealer/guide/features/layout.md
---

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /annealer/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /annealer/llms-full.txt.

# Layout

Reordering attributes can break the original line layout of a tag. The `layout` section of a profile defines how tags are laid out afterwards. Each rule mirrors an eslint-plugin-vue rule, so projects that keep those rules get consistent results.

Both built-in profiles turn `closingBracketNewline`, `oneAttributePerLine` and `selfClosing.void` (`<br />`, `<hr />`, `<wbr />`, …) on. Self-closing empty elements and components (`selfClosing.normal`/`component`) and `contentNewline` rewrite markup beyond what reordering needs, so the built-in profiles define them but leave them off (`enabled: false`). Turn them on when needed:

| Rule             | CLI                 | JavaScript             | Profile                        |
| ---------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `selfClosing`    | `--self-closing`    | `selfClosing: true`    | `selfClosing.enabled: true`    |
| `contentNewline` | `--content-newline` | `contentNewline: true` | `contentNewline.enabled: true` |

The CLI flags and JavaScript options override the profile's `enabled`. `--no-self-closing` / `--no-content-newline` (or `false`) turn a rule off in a profile that enables it.

## `closingBracketNewline`

Equivalent to `vue/html-closing-bracket-newline`. The closing bracket of a multiline start tag goes on its own line. A start tag whose attributes fit on one line keeps `>` on that line (`singleline: never`).

## `oneAttributePerLine`

Equivalent to the multiline default of `vue/max-attributes-per-line`. In a start tag whose attributes span several lines, each attribute goes on its own line.

This is needed because reordering could otherwise put two attributes on one line if attributes kept their original line positions.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->

```html
<!-- Input -->
<div class="a"
  id="x"></div>

<!-- Output -->
<div
  id="x"
  class="a"
></div>
```

## `selfClosing`

Equivalent to `vue/html-self-closing`. Set per element kind, each to `always`, `never` or `preserve`. `void` always applies; `enabled` (off in the built-in `vue` profile, see above) covers `normal` and `component` only:

| Kind        | Example      | Built-in `html` | Built-in `vue` |
| ----------- | ------------ | --------------- | -------------- |
| `void`      | `<br />`     | `always`        | `always`       |
| `normal`    | `<div />`    | –               | `always`       |
| `component` | `<MyComp />` | –               | `always`       |

- `normal` and `component` apply in Vue templates only. In plain HTML, `<div />` is an unclosed start tag.
- Whitespace-only content counts as empty, except in `pre` and `textarea`.
- SFC top-level blocks (`<template>`, `<script>`, `<style>`) are never touched.

:::warning Difference from vue/html-self-closing
`void: always` differs from the default of `vue/html-self-closing` (`html.void: never`). If you keep that ESLint rule, set `html.void: always` there, or `void: never` in your annealer profile.
:::

## `contentNewline`

Equivalent to `vue/multiline-html-element-content-newline`. Off in the built-in profiles (see above). In your own profile, omit the key or set `enabled: false` to turn the rule off; `{}` turns it on with the defaults. `--content-newline` on a profile without the key also uses the defaults.

- An element is **multiline** when its end tag starts on a later line than its start tag (the ESLint rule's definition). Its content then starts and ends with exactly one line break.
- `allowEmptyLines: true` keeps blank lines instead of collapsing them.
- Empty elements are left alone.
- `ignore` lists elements that are left alone, together with everything inside them. The default is the rule's default: `pre`, `textarea` and inline elements (`a`, `span`, `strong`, …), where added whitespace could be visible.
- Unclosed HTML elements (`<li>` without `</li>`) are closed implicitly by an ancestor's end tag and are not touched.
- Only line breaks are added; indentation is not re-flowed. The new line takes the attribute indentation of a multiline start tag, else the first deeper content line, else the tag's indentation plus two spaces (a tab if the tag is indented with tabs).

<!-- prettier-ignore -->

```vue
<!-- Input -->
<template>
  <div class="a"
    id="x"><MyComp></MyComp></div>
</template>

<!-- Output (vue profile, --self-closing --content-newline) -->
<template>
  <div
    id="x"
    class="a"
  >
    <MyComp />
  </div>
</template>
```

The HTML profile defines the rule too. Whitespace at the start and end of block-level content is not rendered, and the `ignore` list covers the elements where it could be.

Moving content to a new line can change the indentation that a nested tag's closing bracket aligns to. annealer therefore formats the document again until it is stable (at most 4 passes, normally 2).



---
url: /annealer/guide/features/class-order.md
---

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /annealer/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /annealer/llms-full.txt.

# Class order

annealer can reorder the classes inside static `class` attributes. The order comes from a **class order profile**, a YAML file separate from the attribute profile, so it can be swapped for another library's order.

It is off by default. Turn it on with a class order name or file:

```bash
anyl --class-order tailwind src/**/*.vue
anyl --class-order ./my-classes.yaml index.html
```

```ts
format(source, { language: 'vue', classOrder: 'tailwind' });
```

An attribute profile can also name one with [`classOrder`](/annealer/api/profile.md#classorder). `--class-order` and the `classOrder` option override it.

## Built-in: `tailwind`

The built-in `tailwind` class order follows the order that `eslint-plugin-tailwindcss` (`classnames-order`) and `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss` apply. Both take it from the Tailwind CSS compiler.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->

```html
<!-- Input -->
<div class="p-3 border-gray-300 m-4 h-24 lg:p-4 flex border-2 lg:m-4 card"></div>

<!-- Output -->
<div class="card m-4 flex h-24 border-2 border-gray-300 p-3 lg:m-4 lg:p-4"></div>
```

annealer doesn't run Tailwind. The order is data, generated from Tailwind CSS 4.3 with its default theme by `scripts/generate-tailwind-order.mjs`. The same script writes a test corpus of 3,000 class lists sorted by Tailwind itself, and annealer's output matches all of them.

Differences from running Tailwind:

- **Your own theme and utilities aren't known.** A custom color (`bg-brand-500`) is ordered like a theme color, because a value that matches no other rule falls back to the color rule. A custom utility (`@utility`) is an unknown class.
- **Duplicates are kept by default.** `eslint-plugin-tailwindcss` removes them by default (`removeDuplicates`). Removing classes is a lint concern, so the built-in profile keeps them. To remove them, pass `--remove-duplicate-classes` (JavaScript: `removeDuplicateClasses: true`) or use a class order with `removeDuplicates: true`. The option also works without a class order: the classes keep their order and only the repeats go.
- **Only static `class` attributes.** `:class` bindings and `clsx()`-style calls are expressions, and annealer never reads them.

## How classes are ordered

1. Classes no rule matches (`card`, `js-toggle`) go first, in their source order (`unknown: end` puts them last).
2. Classes without variants come first. Classes with variants follow, by the ranks of their variants (`variants.order`). The highest rank decides, like comparing bit masks.
3. Then by the CSS properties a class sets: the first property that differs, by its position in `propertyOrder`.
4. Then more properties first (`count`).
5. Then by name, with runs of digits compared as numbers (`p-2` before `p-10`).

This is the comparison Tailwind uses. Nothing in it is specific to Tailwind: any utility library can describe its classes by the properties they set.

## What changes in the markup

- Whitespace stays in place: classes move between the existing separators, so multi-line class lists keep their line breaks.
- Values with template syntax (`{{ }}`, `{% %}`, `<?php ?>`, `${}`) and unquoted values are left as written.
- [Disable directives](/annealer/guide/features/disable-directives.md) apply as for attributes.

## Writing a class order

```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://github.com/logue/annealer/raw/refs/heads/main/crates/annealer/schema/class-order.schema.json
schemaVersion: 1
name: my-utilities
unknown: end
propertyOrder: [display, margin, padding, color]
values:
  size: [sm, md, lg]
rules:
  - match: [d-*]
    properties: [display]
  - match: ['m-{number}', 'm-{size}', mx-auto]
    properties: [margin]
  - match: ['p-{number}']
    properties: [padding]
  - match: [text-*]
    properties: [color]
```

- `match` patterns: `*` matches any run of characters; `{name}` matches one entry of a value set in `values`. `{number}` (a decimal number) is built in.
- The most specific pattern wins: an exact name, then the most literal characters, then the most value sets.
- A modifier after `/` (`bg-red-500/50`) is ignored when the class without it matches better.

See the [class order reference](/annealer/api/profile.md#class-order-profiles) for every key. `builtinClassOrder('tailwind')` in the JavaScript API returns the built-in YAML as a starting point.



---
url: /annealer/guide/features/disable-directives.md
---

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /annealer/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /annealer/llms-full.txt.

# Disable directives

Some code must keep its exact form, for example a third-party snippet or a legacy order kept on purpose. Comments switch annealer off for that code.

```html
<!-- annealer-disable -->
<!-- annealer-enable -->
<!-- annealer-disable-next-line: [reason] -->
```

```css
/* annealer-disable */
/* annealer-enable */
/* annealer-disable-next-line: [reason] */
```

## Rules

- **Block comments only.** `//` is not supported, because CSS has no line comments.
- **`annealer-disable`** covers everything after it, up to `annealer-enable` or the end of the document. At the top of a document, it leaves the file unchanged.
- **`annealer-disable-next-line`** covers the constructs that start on the next line:
  - a start tag (the whole tag, even if it spans several lines, and a `<style>` element's content), or
  - a CSS statement (a declaration or a whole rule).
- **The reason after `:` is optional** and ignored by annealer.
- **Covered code is kept verbatim and in place.** In a stylesheet, covered declarations also stay where they are while their neighbors are sorted.
- **Scope:** markup comments apply to markup (and to whole `<style>` elements). CSS comments apply inside the stylesheet they appear in.
- **Unknown directives are errors.** A comment that starts with `annealer-` but is not a known directive (for example the typo `annealer-disabel`) fails the run instead of being ignored.

```html
<!-- annealer-disable-next-line: copied from the vendor's docs -->
<a href="/" id="vendor-link">Kept as written</a>
<a href="/" id="home">Reordered</a>
```

## Implementation note (stylesheets)

malva's own ignore comment (`malva-ignore`) can't be reused. It rejects the `: reason` form, and sorting still moves the ignored declaration. Instead, annealer marks covered statements with internal markers before calling malva and removes them afterwards.

Sass (indented syntax) has no `;`, so the markers go on lines of their own there. malva honors its ignore comment in Sass only on its own line.



---
url: /annealer/guide/design/value-ordering.md
---

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /annealer/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /annealer/llms-full.txt.

# Value ordering

:::info Status
Both are implemented: static `style` attributes (opt-in, see [Stylesheets](/annealer/guide/concepts/stylesheets.md#static-style-attributes-opt-in)) and `class` values with a swappable class order (see [Class order](/annealer/guide/features/class-order.md)), with a built-in `tailwind` order. A Bootstrap profile is not written yet. This page records the principles behind them.
:::

Attribute order is one axis. The order of the values inside an attribute is another. The need isn't specific to Tailwind: any class-based CSS framework (Bootstrap, Tailwind, a project's own utility set) benefits from a fixed class order, for the same diff-stability reason as attributes.

## Principles

### Static values only

Bound attributes (`:class`, `:style`, `v-bind:*`) hold expressions, not values. annealer never looks inside them.

This differs from `eslint-plugin-tailwindcss` (`classnames-order`) and `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss`, which also sort string literals inside `:class` expressions and `clsx()`-style calls.

### A library-agnostic mechanism, with library-specific profiles

The class order is plain profile data, like attribute groups, not a code branch. This is the first concrete case of [library profiles](/annealer/guide/design/library-profiles.md).

### The library owns its class order

A framework's canonical class order is a design decision of that framework, not of annealer. annealer provides the mechanism and the profile format.

- **Bootstrap**: annealer proposes the mechanism upstream, with a draft profile (Bootstrap 6 is in development), so that Bootstrap itself defines and maintains the order.
- **Tailwind**: the order is already defined by Tailwind's engine. annealer ships it as built-in YAML (`tailwind`), generated from Tailwind and checked against it. It follows the spec of `eslint-plugin-tailwindcss` `classnames-order`, except that duplicates are kept (see below).

### The profile format is a public contract

Third parties are expected to write and ship profiles. Before the proposal, `schemaVersion`, the JSON Schema and the format documentation must be stable. Profiles distributed outside annealer also need a loading path (for example, `extends` resolving a file shipped in a package).

### An approximate, self-contained order

The official Tailwind order is derived from each project's own Tailwind build (v4 `@theme` and custom utilities, v3 `tailwind.config.js`). Only Tailwind itself can compute it. annealer defines the order in YAML instead:

- close to the official order for standard utilities,
- custom utilities are not known,
- no JavaScript runtime is required.

### Never change meaning

Reordering classes doesn't change CSS semantics. Duplicate classes are kept (removing them is a lint concern), and unknown classes are never dropped.

## Design

- **Classes are ranked by the CSS properties they set**, with Tailwind's comparison: unknown classes, variants, the first differing property in a property order, the number of properties, then the name. Properties are library-agnostic, so a Bootstrap profile can use the same format (`d-flex` sets `display`, `mt-3` sets `margin-top`).
- **Variants** (Tailwind's `md:`, `hover:`) are a separate axis: a separator and a ranked list of variant patterns.
- **Patterns** are richer than attribute patterns: `*` anywhere and `{name}` value sets, with the most specific match winning. `text-center`, `text-lg` and `text-red-500` resolve to different rules.
- **The class order is its own profile**, not part of the attribute profile, so it can be combined with any attribute profile: `--class-order`, the `classOrder` option, or `classOrder` in a profile.

## Resolved questions

- Where unknown classes go: `unknown: start` (Tailwind's order) or `end`.
- Whitespace inside a `class` value is preserved: classes move between the existing separators, as `eslint-plugin-tailwindcss` does.

## Open questions

- Infix breakpoints (Bootstrap's `col-md-6`, `d-lg-none`) are not a separate axis yet. A profile can only rank them through patterns.
- How attribute profiles compose (for example `extends: vue`). This also serves library-specific attribute rules.



---
url: /annealer/guide/design/library-profiles.md
---

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /annealer/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /annealer/llms-full.txt.

# Library profiles

:::info Status
Planned. The discovery policy below is decided; the implementation is not done yet.
:::

annealer will support rule settings specific to a library (a UI kit, a CSS framework). These reuse the existing profile mechanism instead of adding code branches:

- attribute groups,
- `layout.selfClosing` per element kind,
- normalization options,
- class value order (see [Value ordering](/annealer/guide/design/value-ordering.md)).

The mechanisms are kept general and data-driven, so a library profile can extend or override them. This will likely need profile composition (`extends`) and per-tag or per-component overrides.

## Discovery policy

### Detected by `annealer.yaml` in the package

A package provides a library profile when its package root contains an `annealer.yaml`. The presence of that file is the only signal. annealer doesn't use package-name conventions and doesn't guess from the package contents.

### Direct dependencies only, by default

Only the project's direct dependencies are scanned. A transitive dependency is included only when a library author opts in explicitly. For example, a UI kit built on Bootstrap can declare in its own `annealer.yaml` that it carries Bootstrap's profile.

A package somewhere deep in the dependency tree doesn't mean the project's markup uses its classes.

### Detection and application are separate

Detection only finds candidates and reports them. A profile is applied only when the user names it explicitly in their config.

Installing or updating a dependency must never change annealer's output by itself.

## Bootstrap

For Bootstrap, the plan is to propose the mechanism to the Bootstrap project (v6 is in development) with a draft profile, so that Bootstrap owns its class order. This requires a stable, documented profile format first.



---
url: /annealer/guide/design/decisions.md
---

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /annealer/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /annealer/llms-full.txt.

# Design decisions

## Architecture

```text
annealer (core)  pure function: format(input: &str, config: &Config)
                   -> Result<String, FormatError>
                 No file I/O. Builds for wasm32-unknown-unknown.
                 Uses malva for CSS/SCSS/Sass/Less declaration order.

anyl (CLI)       File I/O and argument parsing; calls the core.

annealer (npm)   WebAssembly build of the core with a TypeScript wrapper.
```

- **One crate.** The core and the CLI live in one crate (`crates/annealer`) for now. It will be split into a workspace only when a real need appears, to avoid premature abstraction. The CLI's `clap` dependency is behind the default `cli` feature, so the library builds for WebAssembly with `--no-default-features`.
- **Profiles are YAML, not code.** HTML, Vue and future profiles are data. Each profile has `schemaVersion`, because the format is as much a public API as the Rust function signature.
- **Strict validation.** Unknown keys are rejected when the profile is parsed, so typos surface immediately. A JSON Schema (draft-07) is provided for editor support. Two rules that draft-07 can't express (exactly one fallback group, unique group names) are checked only by the loader.
- **malva is pinned loosely** (`0.16`), in line with the library dependency policy used in other projects.
- **The npm package embeds the WebAssembly binary** as base64 instead of shipping a separate `.wasm` file. The cost is about 33% more bytes before compression. In return, `format()` is synchronous and needs no bundler or loader setup.

## Decisions made during implementation

1. **HTML profile order.** The original table had no place for unmatched attributes or for `alt`/`title`. The agreed order is id → class → supplementary (`alt`, `title`, `placeholder`) → semantic (`type`, `href`, `src`, `srcset`) → key-value (`name`, `value`, `content`) → dimensions (`width`, `height`) → other (state: `disabled`, `checked`, …) → ARIA → data → events. The Vue profile uses the same order inside its other-attributes tier.
2. **Static before bound applies to `class` only.** For other names, the cluster keeps the source order, because Vue merges `style` with the later declaration winning and keeps only one value for other duplicates.
3. **`spreadSafe` groups.** Compile-time directives never merge with a `v-bind` spread object, so they may move across spreads. Everything else stays inside its segment.
4. **One attribute per line in multiline tags.** Otherwise reordering could put two attributes on one line. This matches the multiline default of `vue/max-attributes-per-line` and can be turned off with `layout.oneAttributePerLine`.
5. **Vue tier 8 is split** into other directives, then other attributes, as in `vue/attributes-order` (`OTHER_DIRECTIVES` → `OTHER_ATTR`).
6. **`void: always` differs from `vue/html-self-closing`'s default** (`html.void: never`). Projects that keep that ESLint rule need to align one side.
7. **`contentNewline` is defined in the HTML profile too.** Whitespace at the start and end of block-level content isn't rendered, and the `ignore` list covers the elements where it could be.
8. **Vendor-prefixed declarations go first** (`vendorPrefix: start`), so the standard property is declared last and wins. See [Stylesheets](/annealer/guide/concepts/stylesheets.md#vendor-prefixes-vendorprefix-start).
9. **Self-closing empty elements and components, and `contentNewline`, are opt-in.** They rewrite markup beyond what reordering needs, and they conflict with setups that don't use those eslint-plugin-vue rules (Prettier, for example). The built-in profiles keep their settings with `enabled: false`; `--self-closing` / `--content-newline` or the matching JavaScript options turn them on. Void elements (`<br />`) are self-closed always, as Prettier also writes them.

## Resolved questions

- **`v-model` and a plain `value`**: never clustered. The key `v-model` differs from `value`.
- **Profile strictness**: unknown keys are rejected at parse time.
- **malva version**: loose range `0.16`.

## Open items

- Upgrade raffia to 0.13 once malva does (malva 0.16 still uses raffia 0.12).
- Svelte profile.
- [Value ordering](/annealer/guide/design/value-ordering.md) for static `class` attributes (Tailwind approximation, Bootstrap proposal).
- [Library profiles](/annealer/guide/design/library-profiles.md), profile composition (`extends`) and per-tag or per-component overrides.
- Fixtures taken from real projects, in addition to the hand-written ones.

url: /annealer/api/index.md
---

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /annealer/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /annealer/llms-full.txt.

# API overview

annealer has one Rust core and several ways to call it:

| Entry point      | For                                                        | Reference                                     |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `anyl`           | Formatting files from the command line or in CI            | [CLI](/annealer/api/cli.md)                   |
| `annealer` (npm) | Node.js, browsers and bundlers, through WebAssembly        | [JavaScript API](/annealer/api/javascript.md) |
| Profile YAML     | Customizing attribute order, layout and stylesheet options | [Profile reference](/annealer/api/profile.md) |

The Rust function `annealer::format(input, &Config)` is pure: it does no file I/O, which is why the same core runs in the CLI and in WebAssembly.



---
url: /annealer/api/cli.md
---

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /annealer/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /annealer/llms-full.txt.

# CLI

```text
anyl [OPTIONS] [FILES]...
```

Formats each file and prints the result. Reads stdin when no file is given.

## Options

| Option                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-w`, `--write`               | Overwrite files in place. Can't be combined with `--check`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `-c`, `--check`               | Print the paths of files that would change, and exit with status 1 if any would.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `-p`, `--profile <PROFILE>`   | A built-in profile name (`html`, `vue`) or the path to a profile YAML file. Defaults to the built-in profile for each file's language.                                                                                                                                            |
| `--class-order <CLASS_ORDER>` | Order the classes of static `class` attributes: a built-in class order name (`tailwind`) or the path to a class order YAML file. Overrides the profile's `classOrder`.                                                                                                            |
| `--remove-duplicate-classes`  | Drop repeated classes in static `class` attributes, keeping the first. Works with or without `--class-order`. By default the class order's `removeDuplicates` decides (off in `tailwind`). `--keep-duplicate-classes` keeps them.                                                 |
| `--self-closing`              | Self-close empty elements and components in Vue templates (`layout.selfClosing.normal`/`component`, `vue/html-self-closing`): `<div />`, `<MyComp />`. Off in the built-in profiles. `--no-self-closing` turns it off. Void elements (`<br />`) always follow `selfClosing.void`. |
| `--content-newline`           | Put the content of multiline elements on lines of its own (`vue/multiline-html-element-content-newline`). Off in the built-in profiles. `--no-content-newline` turns it off.                                                                                                      |
| `-l`, `--language <LANGUAGE>` | Language of stdin input: `html` (default), `vue`, `css`, `scss`, `sass`, `less`.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `-h`, `--help`                | Show help.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `-V`, `--version`             | Show the version.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

## Languages

The language of a file is taken from its extension:

| Extension                         | Language   | Default profile                   |
| --------------------------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------- |
| `.html`, `.htm`                   | `html`     | `html`                            |
| `.vue`                            | `vue`      | `vue`                             |
| `.css`, `.scss`, `.sass`, `.less` | stylesheet | `html` (its `stylesheet` section) |

Other extensions are reported as unsupported.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning                                                                                                             |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `0`  | Success. With `--check`: no file would change.                                                                      |
| `1`  | With `--check`: at least one file would change.                                                                     |
| `2`  | Error: unreadable file, unsupported file type, invalid profile, invalid input or an unknown `annealer-*` directive. |

When several files are given, annealer formats all of them, reports each error, and exits with `2` if any failed.

## Examples

```bash
anyl src/App.vue                          # print the result
anyl --write src/**/*.vue                 # format in place
anyl --check index.html                   # use in CI
anyl --profile my-profile.yaml page.html  # custom profile
anyl --class-order tailwind src/**/*.vue  # order Tailwind classes
anyl --class-order tailwind --remove-duplicate-classes src/**/*.vue  # and drop repeated ones
anyl --self-closing --content-newline src/**/*.vue  # also apply the optional layout rules
cat App.vue | anyl --language vue         # stdin
```

url: /annealer/api/javascript.md

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /annealer/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /annealer/llms-full.txt.

# JavaScript API

```ts
import {
  builtinClassOrder,
  builtinProfile,
  format,
  init,
  languageFromPath
} from 'annealer';
```

The package is a WebAssembly build of the Rust core with a TypeScript wrapper. It works in Node.js, in browsers and as a UMD build.

The WebAssembly binary (about 1.5 MB, 0.7 MB gzipped) is embedded in the package as base64. No asset loading needs to be configured, and `format()` is synchronous.

## `format(input, options?)`

```ts
function format(input: string, options?: FormatOptions): string;
```

Reorders attributes (HTML, Vue) or declarations (CSS, SCSS, Sass, Less).

- `options.language`: the input language. Default: `'html'`.
- `options.profile`: a built-in profile name (`'html'`, `'vue'`) or the YAML text of a profile. Default: the built-in profile for `language`.
- `options.classOrder`: a built-in class order name (`'tailwind'`) or the YAML text of a class order. Orders the classes of static `class` attributes and overrides the profile's `classOrder`. Default: classes keep their order. See [Class order](/annealer/guide/features/class-order.md).
- `options.removeDuplicateClasses`: `true` drops repeated classes in static `class` attributes, keeping the first, with or without `classOrder`; `false` keeps them. Default: the class order's `removeDuplicates` (off in `tailwind`, and off without a class order).
- `options.selfClosing`: `true` self-closes empty elements and components in Vue templates (`layout.selfClosing.normal`/`component`: `<div />`, `<MyComp />`); `false` turns that off. Default: the profile's setting (off in the built-in profiles). Void elements (`<br />`) always follow `layout.selfClosing.void`.
- `options.contentNewline`: `true` puts the content of multiline elements on lines of its own, with the rule's defaults when the profile has no `layout.contentNewline`; `false` turns it off. Default: the profile's setting (off in the built-in profiles). See [Layout](/annealer/guide/features/layout.md).

Throws an `Error` when the input or the profile is invalid.

```ts
format('<a title="Home" href="/" id="home">Home</a>');
// => '<a id="home" title="Home" href="/">Home</a>'

format(source, { language: 'vue' });
format(source, { language: 'html', profile: yamlText });
format(source, { language: 'vue', classOrder: 'tailwind' });
format(source, { classOrder: 'tailwind', removeDuplicateClasses: true });
format(source, { language: 'vue', selfClosing: true, contentNewline: true });
```

## `init()`

```ts
function init(): Promise<void>;
```

Compiles the WebAssembly module ahead of time without blocking. Optional: `format()` compiles it synchronously on first use.

## `languageFromPath(path)`

```ts
function languageFromPath(path: string): Language | undefined;
```

Infers the language from a file name or path (`.html`, `.htm`, `.vue`, `.css`, `.scss`, `.sass`, `.less`). Returns `undefined` for other extensions.

## `builtinProfile(name)`

```ts
function builtinProfile(name: 'html' | 'vue'): string;
```

Returns the YAML text of a built-in profile, as a starting point for a custom one.

```ts
const yaml = builtinProfile('vue').replace(
  'oneAttributePerLine: true',
  'oneAttributePerLine: false'
);
format(source, { language: 'vue', profile: yaml });
```

## `builtinClassOrder(name)`

```ts
function builtinClassOrder(name: 'tailwind'): string;
```

Returns the YAML text of a built-in class order, as a starting point for a custom one.

## Types

```ts
type Language = 'html' | 'vue' | 'css' | 'scss' | 'sass' | 'less';

type FormatOptions = {
  language?: Language;
  profile?: string;
  classOrder?: string;
  removeDuplicateClasses?: boolean;
  selfClosing?: boolean;
  contentNewline?: boolean;
};

type Meta = {
  version: string;
  date: string;
};
```

`Language`, `FormatOptions` and `Meta` are also exported as values: the extension-to-language map, the default options, and the build metadata.
